title: Multimodal Fairness and Degradation Simulation Playbook
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview

Summary:
This playbook describes the strategy, dashboards, alerting, and operator simulation steps required to detect, simulate, and remediate multimodal workload fairness issues and progressive degradation modes in the Redwood platform. Multimodal fairness here means equitable latency, token-cost, and quality outcomes across tenants and request shapes (text-only, image+text, streaming video transcripts, embeddings-heavy).

Why this doc exists:
- Platform teams need to ensure we don’t regress fairness when introducing new kernel optimizations, quantization, or regional routing.
- Multimodal mixes can expose asymmetric tail-latency behaviors and cache thrash not seen in pure text workloads.
- Simulation-driven validation (synthetic tenants + dashboard guardrails) reduces regressions and informs rollout gates.

When to use this playbook:
1) Before rolling a runtime change that affects attention/kernel selection, batching, or KV cache eviction policies.
2) When onboarding a model variant that supports images or long context.
3) To investigate skewed SLI burns reported by customers or billing anomalies attributable to multimodal traffic.

Metrics & Dashboard Design

Key metrics to surface (SLO‑mapped):
- foreground_p50_latency_ms, foreground_p95_latency_ms, foreground_p99_latency_ms (per model + per workload-type)
- token_cost_per_request_usd (moving 1h/24h windows)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (prefix and response cache, per-tenant cohort)
- batch_size_distribution (median + tail)
- image_decode_cpu_ms and image_preprocess_queue_depth (for image-heavy requests)
- model_swap_rate_per_minute (model version fallbacks)
- quality_regression_rate (per prompt-set / evaluation harness)
- tenant_degradation_score (composite — see table)

Suggested dashboard panels (examples):
- Multimodal Fairness Overview: per-tenant stacked bar of p95 latency + token cost with trend lines and cohort filters (text-only / image+text / embed-heavy).
- Degradation Heatmap: hour-by-hour tenant_degradation_score with annotation overlay for deployments and kernel toggles.
- KV Cache Cohorts: cache hit-rate by prefix length and tenant, with hypothetical reclaim pressure indicator.
- Preproc Backpressure: image_preprocess_queue_depth vs available preprocess workers and mean decode time.
- Economic Impact Panel: estimated incremental $/day by tenant if current degradation persists (uses token_cost_per_request_usd * 24h request volume estimate).

Metric thresholds and alerting matrix (reference):
| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Suggested alert scope | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| foreground_p95_latency_ms | > 400 ms for >15m | > 800 ms for >5m | model + region + workload-type | platform-ops |
| token_cost_per_request_usd (24h increase) | +20% vs baseline | +50% vs baseline | tenant cohort | billing-team |
| kv_cache_hit_ratio | < 0.45 for 30m | < 0.30 for 10m | model shard / cache pool | runtime-team |
| image_preprocess_queue_depth | > 50 queued for 10m | > 200 queued for 5m | global region | infra-oncall |
| quality_regression_rate | > 1% for 1h | > 5% for 30m | model-version | applied-ml |

Note: thresholds should be parameterized per model-family (e.g., high-latency image encoders will have different baselines).

Tenant Degradation Score (composite formula)
- Components: normalized_p95_latency (0-1), token_cost_spike (0-1), cache_miss_penalty (0-1), quality_drop (0-1)
- tenant_degradation_score = 0.4*normalized_p95_latency + 0.25*token_cost_spike + 0.2*cache_miss_penalty + 0.15*quality_drop
- Interpretation: score > 0.6 = high priority; 0.35-0.6 = medium; <0.35 = nominal

Simulation and Validation Playbook (step-by-step)

Goal: Reproduce realistic multimodal fairness scenarios in the operator sandbox, calibrate dashboards and alert rules, and generate validation artifacts for rollout gates.

Preconditions:
- Access to the platform sandbox with synthetic tenant quotas (operator-sandbox account).
- Simulation harness branch: infra/suites/multimodal-sim (see related_pages).
- Baseline SLI snapshot from last 7 days.

Simulation steps:
1) Define workload shapes (1–3) and load profiles:
   a) Text-only baseline: 10 req/s, mean tokens 150, p95 tokens 450.
   b) Image+text mixed: 4 req/s, image size distribution 256x256 (70%), 512x512 (30%), average tokens 80.
   c) Embedding-heavy: 2 req/s, 2048-dim embed requests batched at 64.
2) Create three synthetic tenants in sandbox: cohort-alpha (text), cohort-beta (image+text), cohort-gamma (embed-heavy). Tag requests with tenant_id header.
3) Run baseline load for 2 hours, capture SLI snapshot and assert tenant_degradation_score < 0.2.
4) Inject a degradation vector: enable experimental kernel 'kv-lite-quant' on a subset of nodes (10%) or reduce preprocess worker pool by 60%.
5) Gradually increase traffic skew to 80% image+text across nodes routing to affected kernel for 30 minutes.
6) Capture metrics, confirm dashboard panels reflect early warning thresholds, and run evaluation prompts for quality_regression_rate.
7) If tenant_degradation_score > 0.6 for any cohort, follow the Operator Runbook below.
8) Produce an artifact: simulation report (markdown) with time-series excerpts, alert events, and recommended remediation steps. Attach to deployment PR.

Operator Runbook: immediate actions when simulation or production alerts fire

Scope: runbook for platform-ops on-call and runtime-team engineers.

Emergency triage (first 15 minutes):
1) Acknowledge alert in pager with copy to Slack channel #platform-incidents.
2) Identify scope using dashboard filters: isolate by region, model, and workload-type.
3) Check KV cache pool metrics and model_swap_rate_per_minute for unexpected fallbacks.
4) If image_preprocess_queue_depth is high: scale preprocess workers (k8s HPA or autoscaler), or pause low-priority preprocess jobs.
5) If foreground_p95_latency is high and model_swap_rate is elevated: route traffic away from affected model variant (traffic-shaper rollback), or increase capacity from dedicated pools.
6) If token_cost_per_request spikes without latency increase: run a tokenization audit (look for malformed requests / prompt injection).
7) Open a post-incident document skeleton in the platform runbook space and link simulation artifacts.

Remediation knobs (order of preference):
- Soft routing: move affected tenants to a fallback model variant with lower memory but higher throughput.
- KV cache heal: trigger manual cache warmup for high-tenancy prefixes (operator script: tools/warmup-prefix --tenant <id> --prefix-len 128).
- Preprocess scaling: temporarily increase instance group size for image preprocessers.
- Rollback kernel changes: revert experimental kernel flags using canary DSL if rollout is recent.

Post-incident validation (after immediate remediation):
1) Re-run the targeted simulation shape at 50% reduced intensity for 30 minutes.
2) Confirm tenant_degradation_score returns to <0.35 for all cohorts.
3) Create a short retrospective and attach simulation reproducible steps and artifacts.

Runbook snippets and useful commands
- PromQL examples:
  - p95 latency per model: percentile_over_time(0.95, rate(request_duration_ms_bucket[5m])) by (model)
  - kv cache hit ratio: sum(kv_cache_hits{pool=~".*"}) / sum(kv_cache_requests{pool=~".*"})
- Operator CLI examples:
  - Scale preprocessers: infractl scale --group image-preproc --replicas 8 --region us-west1
  - Warm cache prefixes: tools/warmup-prefix --tenant cohort-beta --rate 50/s --duration 10m

Rollout and Roadmap Integration

Validation gates to add to rollout pipeline (short-term roadmap items):
- Automated sandbox simulation step in PR pipeline: every kernel or runtime change triggers a 30m multimodal sim with fast checks for tenant_degradation_score and kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Dashboard gating: deployment may not proceed to >25% of fleet until no critical alerts in sandbox sim for 2 consecutive runs.
- Cost-aware rollout: if token_cost_per_request_usd increases >15% in sim, deployment must include a compensating batching/quantization profile.

Longer-term roadmap items (Q2–Q4 2026):
- Multimodal benchmark catalog: curated seed prompts and image corpora per model-family with expected SLI baselines.
- Synthetic tenant marketplace: shareable templates to reproduce common customer traffic mixes.
- ML-based anomaly detection for tenant_degradation_score drift and automated safe-rollbacks.

Roles & Ownership
- Runtime-team: owns cache metrics, kernel toggles, and automated canary DSL.
- Platform-ops: owns operator-sandbox maintenance, operator runbooks, and playbook exercises.
- Applied-ML: owns quality_regression_rate detection and evaluation prompt-sets.
- Observability: dashboards and alerting rules, PromQL library and runbook fragments.

Gameday & Retrospective guidance

Gameday exercise outline (quarterly):
1) Run a 2-hour simulated degradation with a planned kernel change, teams observe dashboards and practice routing/rollback steps.
2) Timeboxed objectives: detect & mitigate within 30 minutes; produce a remediation artifact within 90 minutes.
3) Post-game: 60-minute retrospective, capture three improvements (dashboards, thresholds, operator scripts).

Retrospective template (attach to postmortem):
- Incident summary (what happened).
- Root causes (technical + process).
- What went well.
- Action items (owner + due date).
- Simulation replay URL and artifacts.

Appendix: Example simulation report outline
- Title: Multimodal sim — kv-lite-quant canary — 2026-01-07
- Executive summary (2–3 sentences)
- Scope and setup (tenants, load shapes, flags toggled)
- Time-series excerpts (key panels)
- Alerts triggered and timestamps
- Operator actions taken and exact CLI commands used
- Suggested follow-ups (dashboard tweaks, threshold adjustments, longer-term roadmap items)

Related pages and artifacts
- Attach simulation artifacts to the deployment PR and link to evaluation prompt-sets in applied-ml.
- See related_pages in metadata for starting references.

Contact & escalation
- Primary owner: runtime-team (pager: @runtime-oncall)
- Secondary: platform-ops (Slack: #platform-incidents)
- For billing impact or customer-facing issues: paging-billing@redwood-inference.com

Notes
- This playbook is intended to be conservative by default: prefer safe routing and cache heal over aggressive kernel experiments when multimodal traffic share is unknown.
- Regularly review metric baselines when new model families are onboarded; multimodal baselines can shift by architecture and tokenizer.

End of document.
